headline: Recommended approval of 52 Locke Road micro data center and 7 Rectory Road mail center; continued 270 Loudon Road multifamily building.
summary: Reviewed sign applications and several site and building projects. Recommended approval of a micro data center at 52 Locke Road and a mail center at 7 Rectory Road. The 270 Loudon Road building was continued to November 18, 2026.
decisions: Approved the September 1, 2026 meeting minutes as written, with one member abstaining.
Recommended Planning Board approval of an 8-square-foot window sign at 31A South Main St, unanimously.
Recommended Planning Board approval of two signs at 89 North State Street, with a condition to relocate the building wall sign to the business entrance, unanimously.
Recommended Planning Board approval of two freestanding sign panels and a building wall sign at 15 Chenell Drive, unanimously.
Recommended Planning Board approval of wayfinding and monument signs at 124-130 Hall Street, with conditions, unanimously.
Recommended Planning Board approval of a 12.5-square-foot tenant directory sign at 134 Hall Street, unanimously.
Recommended Planning Board approval of a new canopy and two signs at 333 Loudon Road, unanimously.
Recommended Planning Board approval of the micro data center at 52 Locke Road with conditions on generator and fence color; passed, with Member Thorpe abstaining.
Recommended Planning Board approval of the revised St. Paul's School mail and drop off center at 7 Rectory Road, unanimously.
Continued the 270 Loudon Road multifamily building to the November 18, 2026 Planning Board meeting, with revisions to return to the November 3 committee meeting, unanimously.

City of Concord, New Hampshire 
Architectural Design Review Committee 
 October 6, 2026 Minutes - DRAFT 
 
 
 The Architectural Design Review Committee (ADRC) held its regular monthly meeting on October 6, 2026, 
at the second-floor conference room, at 41 Green St, Concord, NH. 
 
Attendees: Co-Chair Jay Doherty, Member Douglas Proctor, Member Ron King, Co-Chair Elizabeth 
Durfee Hengen, Alternate Member Amanda Savage and Member Merle Thorpe 
 
Absent:   Member Claude Gentilhomme 
 
Staff: Alec Bass, Assistant City Planner – Community Planning; Brian Tremblay, Planning and 
Zoning Inspector; and Krista Tremblay, Administrative Technician III 
 
1. Call to Order 
Co-Chair Doherty called the meeting to order at 8:30 a.m. 
 
2. Minutes – Approve meeting minutes from September 1, 2026 
Co-Chair Hengen moved, seconded by Alternate Member Savage to approve the meeting minutes from 
September 1, 2026, as written. All in favor. The motion passed. Co-Chair Doherty abstained due to not 
being present at the meeting.  
 
3. Staff Memorandum 
4. Sign Applications 
4.1 Paulet Boghosian, on behalf of Who Doesn’t Want That and HC Veritas LLC, requests an architectural 
design review recommendation for a new 8-square-foot non-illuminated window sign (SP-0855-2026) at 
31A South Main St in the Central Business Performance (CBP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0209) (2026-
095) 
 
No one is present to represent this application.  
 
The committee had no objections to the sign.  
Member King made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted. Member Proctor seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously.  
4.2 Concord Comprehensive Treatment Center, on behalf of EWT 54 LLC, requests architectural design 
review recommendations for a new 1.5-square-foot non-illuminated building wall sign (SP-0878-2026) 
and a new 10-square-foot non-illuminated freestanding sign (SP-0879-2026) at 89 North State Street in 
the Civic Performance (CVP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0211) (2026-096) 
Member Thorpe arrived at 8:34 a.m. 
Amy Maillet (89 N State St, Concord) is present to represent this application.  
Co-Chair Doherty stated it is straight forward and the hours on the building and not on the door seem 
appropriate.  
Co-Chair Hengen suggested the hours be placed on the door instead of drilling holes in mortar because 
the hours can shift around. Co-Chair Hengen asked if this is for walk-ins or appointments. 
Ms. Maillet responded by appointment. 
Member Thorpe asked if the sign needs to be that big if you took the hours off and put on the door. It is 
not intended to be read from the street.  
Co-Chair Doherty stated the committee has questions about the sign. Co-Chair Doherty suggested to have 
vinyl letters for the glass of the door for the hours.

Architectural Design Review Committee 
 October 6, 2026 Minutes - DRAFT 
 
 
Ms. Maillet stated there is not enough room to do that.  
Co-Chair Hengen asked where is the primary entrance.  
Ms. Maillet explained in the driveway.  
Co-Chair Hengen asked about the name of the business on the sign the word Concord is easy to read on 
the free-standing sign. Where the Comprehensive Treatment Center has a fairly small script and asked if 
that is how they want it.  
Ms. Maillet replied all of the clinics the town name is larger at all of the company's clinics. 
Member Thorpe asked if no one is going to the front door do they need a sign on the curb as it seems 
redundant.  
Member Savage asked if the committee recommends them not to put the hours on the sign attached to the 
front of the building. If they move the sign to the entrance where patients walk in and asked if that would 
need an approval if it is not visible from the driveway.  
Mr. Tremblay it would if it is visible from off the lot.  
Alternate Member Savage made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application 
as submitted with the condition that the building wall sign be relocated to the actual business entrance on 
the side of the building. Member King seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously.  
4.3 Advantage Signs, on behalf of Alera Group and 13-19 Chenell Drive Business, requests architectural 
design review recommendations for two new, externally illuminated freestanding sign panels of 7.03-
square-feet (SP-0864-2026) and 7.9-square-feet (SP-0865-2026), and 1 new 6-square-foot non-
illuminated building wall sign (SP-0866-2026), all to replace existing signage, at 15 Chenell Drive in the 
Office Park Performance (OFP) District. 
Josh Messinger (128 Hall St, Concord) is present to represent this application. Mr. Messinger stated there 
are two carved freestanding signs with gold leaf that match existing signage on the parcel. One is for the 
conference room and one is for the building. A sandblasted wall sign would be placed at the door 
location.    
Co-Chair Doherty noted the first two signs match close to the sign above them.  
Mr. Messinger noted the intent is to match all signs with the company colors.  
Member Savage noted the Cambridge Investment Research and Alera Group asked if the intent is to 
match the blue so it looks uniform from the street and it is to match the blue of Cambridge. 
Mr. Messinger replied yes.  
Co-Chair Hengen stated she is fine with it and looks good.   
Member King made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted. Alternate Member Savage seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously.  
4.4 Spectrum Signs & Graphics, on behalf of Concord Center, LLC, requests architectural design review 
recommendations for 1 new, 40-square-foot non-illuminated monument sign (FS-S1 – SP-0867-2026), 3 
new, 6.2-square-foot non-illuminated wayfinding signs (S-2 – SP0868-2026, S-2D – SP-0872-2026), and 
S-2F – SP-0874-2026), 2 new, 6-square-foot non-illuminated wayfinding signs (S-2 – SP-0870-2026 and 
S-2C – SP-0871-2026), and 1 new 24.1-square-foot non-illuminated wayfinding sign (S-2E – SP-0873-
2026) at 124-130 Hall Street in the Industrial (IS) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0212) (2026-099)

Architectural Design Review Committee 
 October 6, 2026 Minutes - DRAFT 
 
 
Michael Gallagher (97 Eddy Rd #4, Manchester) is present to represent this application. Mr. Gallagher 
stated this is a wayfinding package for the five-building at a commercial property.   
Mr. Bass advised that the application requires zoning board relief. Mr. Bass stated they are here to receive 
their recommendation and recommend the applicant continue their Planning Board approval to next 
month because the Planning Board will not approve if they are non-conforming with zoning. They have 
submitted variance requests for the November Zoning Board of Adjustment.  
Member Savage asked what is the zoning relief requested.  
Mr. Bass noted it is the number of free-standing signs.   
Mr. Tremblay explained it is also the total square footage and what is before the committee is way finding 
signs and two free-standing signs. 
Mr. Bass stated this issue is the size of the way finding signs.  
Mr. Tremblay noted anything under four square feet would be considered a way finding sign and no 
permit required. These signs are over four-square feet at six square feet it brings them into a free-standing 
sign and a required permit. The signs they are seeing today will be visible from off the property.  
Mr. Gallagher stated this is a way finding package that will go through out the property. The material 
using is aluminum. They are trying to make it so the circulation on the property and visibility to make it 
easier for all people entering the property.  
Member Thorpe asked about the graphics at the top of the sign and if it is a company logo with the tree 
branches.  
Mr. Gallagher stated that is a part of the structure of the sign.  
Co-Chair Hengen noted when looking at the signs it is hard to quickly grasp the arrows. Co-Chair 
Hengen asked if they would consider lumping it together with saying buildings 128 and 124 with a single 
arrow.  
Mr. Gallagher noted that was something they considered and it was dismissed because of the 
configuration of the property. Mr. Gallagher stated the colors in the text aligning with a building color. 
For example, building 124 could have a red color for just the number of the building.  
Co-Chair Hengen stated that would help. Co-Chair Hengen suggested moving the exit arrow closer to the 
word "Exit." 
Mr. Gallagher stated that is something they will consider.  
Member King suggested to center the exit and the arrow it will line up with the peak of the tree.   
Mr. Gallagher will take that into consideration. 
Member Thorpe asked if on the building numbers to have the background a key color that is on the map. 
So, when you arrive at 134 the background color is the building color.   
Mr. Gallagher liked that suggestion.  
Alternate Member Savage made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the 
application as submitted with the following conditions: that the exit and associated directional 
arrows be moved closer together on the wayfinding signs; that the property address number and its 
arrow within the wayfinding signs match a designated building color, which matches the site map; 
and a suggestion that building addresses being added to each building have a font or a background 
added of the associated color designation and the appropriate number located around the building. 
Member King seconded.

recommendation for a new 12.5-square-foot non-illuminated freestanding tenant directory sign (SP-0875-
2026) at 134 Hall Street in the Industrial (IS) District.

5. Building Permit Applications

Co-Chair Doherty appreciated the night view.

6. Site Plan Applications 
6.1 Northpoint Engineering, LLC, on behalf of Granite Municipal Manufacturing & Sales, LLC, requests an 
architectural design review recommendation as part of a major site plan approval for the construction of a 
new 8,160-square-foot building for the use as a micro-data center, office, garage, and single residential 
caretaker unit, and associated site improvements at Tax Map 40Z Lot 6, addressed as 52 Locke Road in 
the Industrial (IN) and Open Space Residential (RO) Districts. (PL-SPR-2026-0066) (PL-CUP-2026-
0126) (2026-087) 
Jeff Lewis (119 Storrs St Suite 201, Concord) and Michael Trahan (674 Old Walpole Rd, Surry) are
City of Concord, New Hampshire 
Architectural Design Review Committee 
 October 6, 2026 Minutes - DRAFT 
 
 
present to represent this application. Mr. Lewis stated he was before the committee in the spring for this 
parcel and a completely different project was proposed. Mr. Lewis noted they have decided to go into a 
different direction. Mr. Lewis stated this will be a micro data center. There will be back up generators. 
There dry coolers for the heating and cooling for the building. This will be a secure facility as it will be 
secured with a fence and gate. There are no public that will enter into the facility. There will be a 
caretaker apartment and garage for 24/7 on-site security. There will be occasional maintenance at the 
facility.  
Member King asked about the noise that will be generated.  
Mr. Lewis replied not a lot. The only noise would be when the dry coolers kick on. It is an emerging 
cooling system which is new technology. The heat will be recaptured and used to heat the building.  
Co-Chair Doherty asked how tall are the dry coolers and the generators.  
Mr. Lewis responded 96 inches.  
Member Thorpe asked about decibel levels for the variable-speed coolers and the generators, and about 
their cumulative effect near wildlife areas.  
Mr. Trahan stated they are low RPM variable speed acoustic fans designed for quiet operation.   
Mr. Lewis said noise data was submitted for the Planning Board application and that technical experts 
will attend that hearing.  
Co-Chair Doherty noted the building was painted dark to make it disappear. However, the generator 
boxes are a silver.  
Member Thorpe suggested to have an acoustical surrounding fence around the perimeter of the property 
to contain or muffle the sound.  
Mr. Bass stated that noise impacts are generally outside the committee's purview, which covers fencing, 
elevations, landscaping, and site appearance.  
Co-Chair Hengen asked if there is any visibility of the building from interstate 93.  
Member Proctor replied possibly in the winter time with the leaves gone.  
Member Savage stated there is a good distance between 93 and this property.   
The Committee members agreed the dark building color was acceptable and the generators should be a 
dark, matte color.  
Co-Chair Doherty asked whether the caretaker unit could use the building's volume, such as a loft with a 
bed area.  
Mr. Trahan replied possibly.  
Member Thorpe asked about the lighting around the fixture locations and asked if they are not directed 
towards the wildlife.  
Mr. Lewis replied the lighting is all pack lighting for security. 
The committee has no comments on the building itself.  
Member Thorpe asked about the fencing height and material.  
Co-Chair Doherty noted the plan states eight-foot height.  
Mr. Lewis replied chain link fence.  
Co-Chair Hengen suggested a dark chain.

submitted with the following conditions: that the generators have a dark color exterior cladding

Discussion 
Member Thorpe asked that the decibel information be available before the Planning Board.  
Mr. Bass agreed to carry that request forward. 
All in favor. The motion passed. Member Thorpe abstained from voting.  
6.2 Wilcox & Barton, Inc, on behalf of St. Paul’s School, requests an architectural design review 
recommendation as part of a major site plan approval for the construction of a new 2,208-square-foot 
building, for the use as a mail and drop off center, serving the St. Paul’s School campus, along with 
associated site improvements at Tax Map 723Z Lot 13-1, addressed as 7 Rectory Road in the 
Institutional (IS) District.(PL-SPR-2026-0067) (PL-CUP-2026-0129) (2026-091) 
Erin Lambert (2 Home Ave, Concord) and Brian Apito (75 Central St, Boston) are present to represent 
this application. Ms. Lambert presented a revised plan that differs from the committee's packet. The 
applicant will go to the November Planning Board and sought feedback in the interim. They do not need 
as much parking so they have a revised site plan. The revised site plan reduces impervious pavement by 
right-sizing parking on the site of an existing parking lot, reserves a turnaround, and adds walkways. The 
building has been shifted to be closer to Dunbarton Road. The building will be for food delivery services 
for students and staff to pick up. They only need enough pavement for two delivery trucks. They are 
applying for a conditional use permit application to reduce the parking.    
Mr. Apito stated the building footprint was reduced to approximately 1,850 square feet. It is a one-story 
building with a gable roof and shed dormer. It contains a smart-locker package pickup area, reception, 
back-of-house storage, a limited-hours food delivery pickup area (7 to 9 PM), and a separate side entry 
for contractor and visitor check-in under a wraparound porch. The materials include composite siding and 
trim, a standing seam metal roof, wood-clad windows with simulated divided lights, and stained douglas 
fir columns and beams. Site lighting will match campus light poles. 
Co-Chair Hengen asked if there will be expressed exterior muttons.  
Mr. Apito replied yes, similar to vinyl.  
Co-Chair Hengen asked about the columns.  
Mr. Apito responded they will be stained and pressure treated underneath.  
Member Thorpe liked how the building fits the agricultural character of the nearby barn. Member Thorpe 
noted the bank to the south of the building is a great place to sit to over see the playing fields. Member 
Thorpe asked if they gave thought to installing trees across the bank to shade while watching.   
Mr. Apito replied that is something they can bring to St. Paul’s. They do not want to have too many sight 
lines from the new admissions building and the porch view of the fields.  
Ms. Lambert noted the sight line for the admissions and would not be able to put trees directly in front.   
Co-Chair Doherty noted they are not going to Planning Board until November and they are asking for the 
committee approval now. 
Ms. Lambert stated that would be great however, she recognizes that they did not have a chance to see the 
site or the updated plans. If they can give their thoughts on the building.  
Co-Chair Doherty noted what is in the packet is not what they are showing and they need what was

6.3 Gallagher Callahan & Gartrell PC and Jones & Beach Engineers, Inc, on behalf of Onyx Partners, Ltd and 
Onyx Steeplegate Concord, LLC, requests an architectural design review recommendation as part of a 
major site plan approval for the construction of a 4-story, 133,600-gross-square-foot, 110-unit 
multifamily building and associated site improvements at Tax Map 611Z Lot 40, addressed as 270 
Loudon Road in the Gateway Performance (GWP) District. (PL-SPR-2026-0068) (PL-CUP-2026-0130) 
(PL-CUP-2026-0130) (2026-092) 
Doug Richardson (40 Franklin St, Needham MA), Ian McKinnon (100 Dominic Dr Suite 201, Exeter) 
and Joe Ford are present to represent this application. Mr. Richardson noted the first residential building 
of a 600-unit master plan at the former Steeplegate Mall site. The design was reduced from a five-story, 
structured-parking building to a four-story, 110-unit building with surface parking at 1.5 spaces per unit. 
There are 50 two bedroom, 50 one bedroom and 10 studio apartments. This building will take 18 months 
of construction. They are timing it to be completed with the two large retail anchors to the west. There is a 
traffic study as part of the CDP. They have received staff and state DOT comments. It is a wood-frame 
building with real thin brick, Hardy panel, lap siding, and double-hung windows. The first floor includes 
about 7,500 square feet of amenity space, a leasing office, small fitness, Amazon room and a pool area 
with fencing and security access.

Mr. Richardson stated it would be black aluminum to look like a rot iron fence.  
Member Savage asked for screening for all of the meters.  
Mr. Richardson noted the intent for the electric meters is to put them in a large room.  
Mr. Richardson noted the site plan cannot be approved before the CDP is approved.  
Member King felt the site layout and pedestrian are hemmed in by the parking and the building's 
proximity to it.  
Member Thorpe noted there are two little trees planted along the entire length of the building. Member 
Thorpe suggested to have one parking space further away to allow for landscaping.  
Mr. Richardson stated this is not a suburban apartment project. This is an urban mixed feel.   
Mr. McKinnon noted the CDP is active and will be before the Board. Mr. McKinnon noted this is phase 
one. Mr. McKinnon stated there is a street scape and separated sidewalk. There will be an eight-foot 
multiuse path that will go along all of the project surround Loudon Road and D’Amante Drive. There is a
